newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end higher, Bombay index up 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end higher, Bombay index up 1.4 pct.

text.p: ** (1215 GMT) - Indian shares stage smart rally, operators
build up positions in new account at Bombay bourse
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram says reduction in
** Recent decline in short-term interest rates could
influence other, longer maturities to fall, RBI
governor says after meeting Finance Minister
** Thomas Cook announces two bonus shr for every three held
** Delhi index up 14.23 pts at 789.93 provisional, Madras
index 6.37 pts and National index 2.50 pts at 1072.60
Shares at major Indian exchanges ended mostly higher on Monday, but the sharp gains were concentrated in blue chips stock and showed no signs of percolating to the broader market, dealers said.
"People would like to stay long, but the market still lacks widespread buying," said a dealer at a Bombay foreign brokerage. "Foreign funds are not aggressive buyers," he said.

The BSE index ended 52.81 points higher at 3,798.12 after shedding nearly 3.4 percent last week. Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told the central bank on Monday that interest rates should be reduced to support economic growth.
